feedback: Build the cargo box, called box, as a solid block standing in for the foam box: 74 in wide (centred on y = 0), 39 in deep and 41 in high, its front face at x = -18 in (so it runs back to x = -57 in), its flat floor at z = 12 in, resting on top of the ladder. Make it tunable for a drag study: besides width, depth, height, x_front and z_bottom, give PARAMS tail_len, tail_drop, tail_pinch and tail_edge_r, all 0 so it starts as a plain box. tail_len is how much of the back tapers, tail_drop how far the top falls by the very back, tail_pinch how far each side draws in by the very back, tail_edge_r the rounding of the back's top and side edges (0 = sharp). Build the taper as flat panels (a ruled loft) and keep the bottom flat. It must clear the hatch swing by at least 2 in.

feedback: The frame now has a riser: raise the box so its floor is at 18 in (z_bottom = 18 in), resting on top of the ladder. Change nothing else. The box must stay seated on the frame, touching it.

Rebuild cargo_box as a camper shell with a teardrop tail. Keep: the floor is a flat, full 74 x 39 in rectangle at z = 18 in (a mattress goes on it), the front face is flat at x = -18 in, it is 41 in tall and centred on y = 0. Build it as a smooth loft (ruled=False) through cross-sections in the YZ plane: one at the front face, one where the tail starts, and 8 evenly spaced through the tail to the back at x = -57 in; if tail_len is under 1 in, just make the plain box. Each cross-section is a six-sided outline: the full-width floor edge, straight vertical side walls up to wall_h above the floor, then upper side panels leaning in to a roof that is narrower on each side by tail_pinch * t**tail_curve, at a height of height - tail_drop * t**tail_curve above the floor (never lower than wall_h + 1 in). t is 0 ahead of the tail and runs from 0 to 1 over the last tail_len of the box. PARAMS in mm with inches in comments: width 74 in, depth 39 in, height 41 in, x_front -18 in, z_bottom 18 in, wall_h 12 in, tail_len 0, tail_drop 0, tail_pinch 0, tail_curve 1. tail_curve 1 means straight panels; 2 means a curved teardrop roof that starts tangent to the flat roof.

The smooth loft overshoots: with tail_curve 1 the roof bulges about 1.4 in above the 41 in height where the flat roof meets the tail. Build the front part as a plain extrusion of the full section from the front face back to where the tail starts, loft (ruled=False) only through the tail's sections, starting at that same section, and union the two. Keep everything else, including PARAMS.
